AUDIT (AC4) — binding_recovery.py:342-346 pending-recovery loop vs the per-JQL search memo:

FINDING: unaffected by the memo; no change needed.

Proof:
1. WITHIN a pass, the loop issues each JQL once per pending id: the primary 'labels = "rebar-id:<local_id>"' and the hyphen fallback are DISTINCT JQL strings, so neither can replay the other's cached answer, and neither is re-asked in the same pass.
2. ACROSS passes, search_miss_count corroboration accumulates toward _MISSES_BEFORE_UNBIND — but each pass constructs a fresh client (and thus a fresh memo): reconcile_helpers.bind_operation_runtime (reconcile_helpers.py:675) composes 'the ONE operation runtime for this pass' per pass; _backend_registry.select_backend (_backend_registry.py:60-76) constructs a fresh backend on every call with no caching; the production entrypoint runs one reconcile_once per process (__main__.py:450). So repeated misses are genuinely fresh queries — the unbind threshold can never be satisfied by replays of one cached negative.

This lifetime proof is also recorded at the cache definition in acli.py (AcliClient.__init__, change 2146).
